messages:
Alex: Heads-up: scheduling a quiet-hour maintenance in us-west2 next Tue 02:00-04:00 UTC. Plan is a preemptive node-label rebalance to consolidate GPU-backed pods and a rolling reboot of affected physical hosts. Expect ~20 nodes cordoned and rebooted in 5 batches of 4.
Sam: ETA on exact start? any planned traffic migration?
Alex: Start 02:00 UTC. We'll route traffic off the cordoned nodes and shift model-serving to burst pools and a small set of dedicated hosts. Routing will be handled by the traffic router; fallback to smaller quantized models enabled for risky routes.
Maria: What's the impact on hosted API SLAs? Do we need to announce to customers?
Alex: Short term: small chance of token latency spikes during a batch (2-3 min) while KV caches rebuild. Error rate should remain low due to rolling design and auto-retries. Ops recommends a customer notification only if latency > 250ms above baseline; otherwise internal comms + support note.
Kevin: How are we hedging capacity? can we pre-warm any caches to lower spike risk?
Maria: We can pre-seed prefix caches and KV caches on backfill nodes. Suggest running the kv-seed job 30m before each batch. Also enable continuous-batch window config to reduce per-token cold penalty.
Alex: Agree. Plan:
1) 01:20 UTC — create canary cordon (2 nodes) and run kv-seed: `kubectl -n inference run kv-seed --image=redwood/kv-seeder -- /bin/seed --pool canary`
2) 01:40 UTC — verify canary latency + model outputs, metrics: RPS, p50/p95, kvcache-hit-rate
3) 02:00 UTC — start batch 1 (4 nodes): cordon, drain, reboot, uncordon, run kv-seed on the replacements
4) repeat every 15m for remaining batches
Sam: Can we temporarily bump capacity in dedicated pools to avoid customer throttles? cost impact?
Alex: Yes, we have burst capacity in dedicated pools. Expected extra cost ~0.6% of monthly infra spend if used fully during the window. Ops is ok with that tradeoff for lower user-visible impact.
EngOps: I'll pre-authorize burst for that window and set alerts for spend > 1% threshold: `alerts set spike-infra-cost --threshold 1% --window 1h`.
Oncall Bot: scheduled_maintenance created: id=sm-2025478901234, start=2025-07-15T02:00:00Z, channels=[#eng-infra,#support], pagerduty=notify-on-high-error-rate
Maria: Two extra asks: (1) Add a routing fallback to model-variant-small for the top 3 high-throughput customers during each batch, (2) ensure any canary inference jobs have consistent random seeds so evals are comparable.
Alex: Noted. I'll push a router change: `curl -X POST https://router.internal/config -d '{"fallback":"variant-small","targets":["custA","custB","custC"]}'` (will use safe deploy with canary=10%).
Kevin: During drain, we'll see ephemeral disk cleanup; watch for pod restarts due to local-data eviction. Ops: add 5m to drain timeout in cordon script: `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=300 --timeout=10m`
Sam: Anyone want to own smoke checks post-batch? I'll take batch 1+2 validation (latency, errors, model-quality quick eval).
Maria: I'll take batch 3+4 verification and run the kv-seed job for those.
Kevin: I'll run the final backfill and confirm uncordon + capacity metrics.
Alex: Thanks. Runbook links: https://internal/redwood/maintenance/runbooks/node-label-rebalance and checklist in #eng-infra pinned.
EngOps: I'll post a support blurb and set a micro-announce to customers on the low-likelihood impact path.
Oncall Bot: reminder scheduled 30m before start -> posting to #eng-infra and @support.
Alex: If we see >2% error rate or p95 > 800ms for more than 3m, abort and rollback routing changes. Pager duty will escalate per runbook.
Sam: Copy that. I'll watch dashboards. :eyes: 
Maria: Adding a quick sanity script here for post-batch smoke test:
```
#!/bin/bash
set -e
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" "https://api.internal/health?model=baseline" | grep 200 || exit 1
# run small prompt eval and compare embedding cosines
```
Kevin: LGTM. See you in the preflight channel at 01:30 UTC.
Alex: Thanks all — I'll update the scheduled maintenance ticket with owners and the cost note. :thumbsup:
